title: Rate Limiter Sliding Window With Per-Entity Limits
statementHtml:
Problem statement

Source note: The judged task is backed by nine earlier author-written Roblox interview reports and a Sep 2, 2026 source slide. The slide directly supports simultaneous per-user and per-experience limits, one shared cap, accepted-only accounting, and exclusion of denied requests. It omits the exact window-endpoint convention, so the practice uses (t - windowLength, t]; its boolean result is represented as 1/0 integers by the runner. The judged task matches the available source at about 95%.

You are given a stream of requests in chronological order. Each request has a timestamp, a user id, and an experience id.

A request is accepted only when both of these limits still have capacity:

  • the number of accepted requests for the same user inside the active sliding window
  • the number of accepted requests for the same experience inside the active sliding window

Only accepted requests count toward future capacity. Denied requests are not stored. For a request at timestamp t, the active window is (t - windowLength, t], so accepted requests at timestamps less than or equal to t - windowLength are expired before checking the new request.

Return an integer array where 1 means the corresponding request is accepted and 0 means it is denied.

signature: rateLimiter(requestTimestamps: int[], userIds: int[], experienceIds: String[], windowLength: int, maxRequests: int) → int[]
constraints: requestTimestamps is sorted in nondecreasing order.
